subject: Dedicated capacity SKU recommendation — Nimbus pilot
messages:
From: Jamal Ahmed <jamal@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai; marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priya@nimbusanalytics.com, cloudops@nimbusanalytics.com

Subject: [Nimbus] Pilot sizing questions — 50-node pilot / perf targets

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

Thanks for taking time last week. We are getting our procurement + infra aligned for the 50-node Dedicated pilot (DEAL-8472). A few specifics we want your recommendation on so we can move to SOW:

- Workloads: mix of embedding/semantic search (70% of QPS) and chat/instructional generation (30%).
- Model targets: SMALL: 7B distil-ish models for session recall + embeddings; MED: 40B MPT-style; LARGE: 70B decoder-only for advanced summarization. We may eventually add a 130B for batch jobs but not in pilot.
- Typical context length: 2k tokens for MED/LARGE; embeddings payload small.
- Traffic: baseline 400 qps with 95th-percentile spikes to 1.4k qps during business hours.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 250ms for SMALL/MED; we can tolerate up to 600ms for LARGE batch summary requests.
- Cost sensitivity: want a pilot that demonstrates unit-cost savings vs our current cloud setup.

I attached our capacity_model.xlsx with per-endpoint QPS.

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Jamal Ahmed <jamal@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-07-21T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [Nimbus] Pilot sizing questions — 50-node pilot / perf targets

Jamal — thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Quick summary up front, then a proposed hybrid SKU plan (high level) and next steps. Attachment: h100-vs-a100-l4-metrics.pdf (benchmarks + cost model).

Executive takeaway (recommended):  run a small hybrid fleet for the pilot rather than a single SKU. That lets Nimbus validate latency-sensitive 70B traffic on H100-class instances while getting cost-efficient steady-state throughput from A100/L4.

Recommended pilot pool (50 nodes equivalent):
- H100-class (4 nodes): reserved for 70B interactive traffic and highest-memory quantized checkpoints. H100s reduce tail latency on long-context requests and improve FP16/FP8 throughput for very large seq lengths.
- A100-80GB (18 nodes): primary workhorses for 40B/70B quantized inference where memory and NVLink matter. Best balance of per-token cost vs model capacity.
- L4 or equivalent serving instances (28 nodes): for embeddings, small 7B models, and high-concurrency low-latency paths. L4s are much cheaper per-inference and reduce queueing for cheap requests.

Why this split? A few concrete tradeoffs:
- Memory headroom: 70B with 2k context in quantized form (4-bit/8-bit) still benefits from 80GB+ VRAM for stable KV cache management — A100-80GB fits most of those profiles but H100 helps with very bursty large-context tails.
- Latency: mixed batching strategy; L4 pool handles tiny-batch sub-50ms responses. A100 handles medium batch sizes with good amortized kernel efficiency. H100 reduces worst-case tail for long sequences that would otherwise push A100 CPU-side scheduling.
- Cost: per-hour cost (relative): H100 >> A100 > L4. The hybrid keeps most traffic on A100/L4 while providing H100s as fast fallback for SLA-sensitive flows.

Sizing rationale (back-of-envelope):
- Baseline 400 qps with 70% embeddings (280 qps): L4 pool sized to sustain 400 concurrent lightweight embedding calls with headroom — 28 nodes covers concurrency and cache-localization for common prefixes.
- MED/LARGE (120 qps combined baseline, spikes to 420 qps): A100s provisioned to serve median traffic; H100s cover 95th spikes for LARGE.

Operational notes / constraints:
- Autoscaling: we recommend enabling burst capacity (on A100 pool) for 2x peak to avoid throttles during launch events.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching will reduce H100 exposure for repeated long contexts; ensure you opt into our prefix-cache config in the SOW.
- Quantization: recommend 4-bit GPTQ for 40B models; 8-bit fallback for 70B if you need more stability during the pilot.

Next steps:
1) Dev/CloudOps share exact VM topology and whether you prefer single-socket H100 instances vs multi-GPU nodes.
2) We’ll produce a costed pilot proposal (node counts + monthly committed capacity) and a MAP (Mutual Action Plan).
3) Quick PoC: 2-week run with instrumented traces; we’ll collect token-level cost and tail latency.

I'll attach the benchmark PDF with per-GPU tokens/sec for the model families you listed. @Dev, can you validate the quantization fallback and whether we want to recommend H100 NVLink clusters or single-socket H100s for Nimbus?

— Rishi

Jamal — appreciate the detail. A couple quick commercial notes while Rishi and Dev validate the stack:

- We can structure the pilot as a 3-month committed capacity with an option to convert to an annual Dedicated contract. That gives you predictable unit pricing for A100/H100/L4 tiers.
- For pricing, two levers matter: committed node-months and burst allowance. For a hybrid pool like Rishi suggested, we typically price the A100 pool at the committed tier and the H100s as a smaller reserved supplement. L4 capacity can be metered as variable usage or reserved if you want cost predictability.

Requested from Nimbus: if you can confirm the % of traffic that must meet the 250ms SLO (vs tolerated 600ms), we can size the H100 headroom more tightly and likely reduce the H100 node count for the pilot.

I'll follow up with a short contract outline and preliminary numbers once we get the technical confirmation.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SKU recommendation — Nimbus pilot

Folks — quick clarifications after reviewing the benchmark PDF and our internal ops constraints: 

- SLO split: 80% of inbound generation traffic must meet 250ms 95th; the remaining 20% are batchy summarizations (600ms ok). That implies tighter H100 headroom.
- VM topology: we prefer 1 x H100 NVLink 80GB per node (single GPU nodes) for reduced scheduling complexity. Our cloud ops team prefers single-socket cards for historic reliability.
- Growth: expect 30% qps increase month-over-month during pilot if pilots go well.

Attaching an updated capacity_model.xlsx with our revised QPS. Can you produce an updated node-level recommendation and an expected monthly committed cost estimate? Also include a MAP with milestones (SOW, PoC start, evaluation date, conversion trigger).

Thanks — Jamal
Jamal Ahmed
VP Product & Cloud Engineering | Nimbus Analytics

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity SKU recommendation — Nimbus pilot

Jamal — great, thanks for the SLO split and the VM preference. Updated notes and immediate action items below. Attachment: Nimbus-MAP-v1.docx (initial mutual action plan).

Updated pilot recommendation (50-node equivalent, costed):
- 1) H100 single-socket nodes: 3 nodes (reserve) + burst pool of 1 node. Given your 80% SLO demand and single-socket preference, we can reduce H100 count to 3 reserved and rely on autoscale to add the burst node during unexpected peaks.
- 2) A100-80GB: 20 nodes reserved. These will handle the bulk of MED traffic and act as primary serving layer for quantized 40B models.
- 3) L4 family: 26 nodes reserved for embeddings + 7B family.

Why the slight shift: your 80% SLO at 250ms reduces the need for many H100s — A100s can handle most steady-state MED traffic with careful quantization and request coalescing. H100s become targeted fallbacks for longest-context interactive flows and very high-percentile spikes.

Estimated committed monthly cost (rough order of magnitude):
- H100 nodes (3 reserved + 1 burst): $XXX,XXX/month (reserve pricing applied)
- A100-80GB (20 nodes): $YYY,YYY/month
- L4 (26 nodes): $ZZ,ZZZ/month

(Dev will replace XXX/YYY/ZZZ with exact numbers once we confirm your cloud-region pricing; this is a preliminary commercial structure.)

Immediate action items:
- Dev: validate quantization fallback plan and confirm expected tokens/sec per GPU with single-socket H100 topology.
- Priyom: generate the pilot commercial terms (3-month committable, burst rules, conversion credits).
- Jamal: confirm target PoC start date (we recommend Aug 10 start to allow provisioning).

I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up to walk through the MAP and the cost table. Thanks everyone — we can turn these numbers into a small SOW and DocuSign package once we lock region pricing.

— Rishi
